key_insight: Stochastic mid-circuit measurements and resets can drive a noisy quantum processor into reproducible non-equilibrium steady states, and those steady states can be modeled quantitatively.
engineering_relevance: This provides a hardware-valid protocol for preparing and studying collective stationary states on near-term superconducting quantum devices, with direct relevance to mid-circuit measurement-based algorithms.
method: Built a noisy discrete-time theory with unitary gates alternating with noisy mid-circuit projective measurements and conditional resets.
Implemented the protocol on a superconducting quantum processor for up to 7 qubits.
Used the interacting Floquet transverse-field Ising model as the benchmark dynamical system.
evidence_signal: The stationary state predicted by the noisy conditional-resetting theory matches the experimental results quantitatively and shows crossover behavior tied to the model’s equilibrium quantum phase transition.
watch_item: The results are demonstrated only up to 7 qubits and depend on realistic noise in mid-circuit measurement/reset operations, so scaling and error sensitivity remain key concerns.
paper_title: Nonequilibrium steady states induced by stochastic mid-circuit measurements and resets on a quantum computer
